headline: Trump said shut the golf course. A judge said no.
summary: A federal judge Saturday stopped the Trump administration from closing East Potomac Golf Links in Washington. Trump had said the 106-year-old public course would shut from November 15 for a 15-month rebuild. Judge Ana Reyes wrote that the government broke at least two laws to meet an arbitrary deadline. Her order runs to November 28.

cover_question.q: Can a judge tell Trump no?

cover_answer: On this, yes. The course stays open until at least Nov. 28.
table_question: Who should decide what happens to a park everyone uses?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The president wants to rebuild an old golf course in Washington and close it for more than a year while the work is done. A judge said he can't shut it yet, so people can keep playing there for now. The course is two miles from the White House, about a 40-minute walk. Nobody is in trouble, and nothing changes for you.
5-7.why: A game that keeps going is the whole story. The 40-minute walk puts the course somewhere real.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script puts the course somewhere real, a 40-minute walk from the White House, and gives one outcome: people keep playing. Expect "why does the president want it?" He likes golf and says the old course is falling apart. The judge said the law comes first.

8-12.script: President Trump wants to rebuild a 106-year-old public golf course in Washington and said it would close Sunday for 15 months. A judge stopped him Saturday, like a referee blowing the whistle until the rule gets checked. She said the government broke at least two laws to meet a deadline it set itself.
8-12.why: A deadline the government set itself is a fairness call they'll make on their own.
8-12.why_long: At ten, fairness is whether adults follow their own rules, and the chain here is a lawsuit in February, trees cut on 15 hours' notice in October, a closure announced anyway, a whistle from the judge. Expect "can he just ignore her?" He could try. She has already opened an inquiry into whether government lawyers misled her.

13-17.script: Can a judge tell Trump no? Here, yes: Judge Ana Reyes blocked the closure Saturday and wrote that the government broke at least two laws to meet an arbitrary deadline. Trump calls the course "Trash Island". Second: if the rebuild would be better, does it matter how he gets there?
13-17.why: A better course against the rule of law. Let them pick a side first.
13-17.why_long: A sixteen-year-old can hold two true things: the course might come out better, and the government broke the law getting there. The script asks whether the end justifies the route. Reyes took 30 pages on it. Expect "what happens on November 28?" The judge decides whether to extend the order.

5-7.a: Not yet. A judge said it has to stay open at least until November 28 while the court looks at the plan.

8-12.q: Why did they cut down the trees?
8-12.a: To start the rebuild. They told the judge 15 hours before. She said stop.
The public. The National Park Service runs it.

13-17.q: Can a judge tell Trump no?
13-17.a: On this, yes. She found the government broke at least two laws.

13-17.q: Isn't a nicer course a good thing?
13-17.a: Maybe. The judge's point: get there by following the law.
